answer: A per-identity collateral lock is what holds Sybil swarms back: every account must bond real tokens before it can mine or grade. An attacker who wants to wander through a thousand addresses must fund a thousand separate locks, and that capital sits idle and slashable the whole time. Since payouts are capped per identity, each extra account adds cost without adding yield, so the farm bleeds while one honest miner keeps its velvet balance. Every new garden of keys multiplies the upfront spend, and collusion detection can freeze the cluster.
